Its whole value is one\nrule; internalize it before anything else:\n\n> **A claim is a FACT only when a deterministic oracle fires over data a real target\n> produced.** You (the LLM) ADVISE where to look and what a result might mean; the oracle\n> CONFIRMS. Nothing else — not your confidence, not a critic's endorsement, not a plausible\n> story — promotes a claim to a fact.\n\nThe standing doctrine every reasoning call operates under is\n[framework/cognitive/metacognition.md](../../../framework/cognitive/metacognition.md) (it is\ninjected into every LLM system prompt). The full architecture — agents, event spine, veracity\nlayer, learning/metacognition core, safety stack — is\n[framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md](../../../framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md). The binding\nconstitution is [CLAUDE.md](../../../CLAUDE.md); never relax scope, destruction, evidence, or\nhonesty rules.\n\n## The invariants (never violate these)\n\n1. **Oracle authority.** Only a fired oracle confirms. Critics/RL/reflection/self-consistency\n   may only *advise, re-rank, defer, or abstain* — never promote a finding or override the oracle.\n2. **Coverage.** Never silently skip an authorized attack surface. Learning and reflection\n   *deprioritise* (re-rank / defer); they never gate a surface out.\n3. **Prove by re-execution.** A finding is a fact only if its retained `oracle_context`\n   re-fires. The veracity firewall (`framework/v2/veracity/`) re-runs proofs; it can only demote.\n4. **Non-circular learning.** An EXPLOITABLE label needs ≥2 independent corroborating oracle\n   kinds; a silent oracle is never auto-labelled a false positive.\n5. **Refuse honestly, fail closed.** Decline to conclude what you cannot ground; record every\n   refusal as evidence. Hard limits (scope, authorization, destruction, real user data) are\n   inviolable — when unsure, stop and ask.\n6. **Determinism + append-only.** No wallclock/global-rng in learning/reward math; the event\n   spine is append-only (supersede, never edit).\n\n## Structured workflows\n\n### Run an authorized engagement (end-to-end, gated)\n1. Confirm the active target's `targets/<slug>/charter.md` authorizes it (constitution §II).\n2. `python3 -m framework.v2 engage <slug> <seed-url> [--recon] [--spine]`\n   — crawls, audits, confirms via oracles, chains attack paths, scores confidence, and\n   (with `--spine`) mirrors the whole run onto the immutable blackboard event stream.\n   (`--strict-evidence` is a **`scan`**-only flag, below — not an `engage` flag.)\n3. Every request passes the full gate chain; an out-of-scope seed or tripped kill-switch\n   refuses *before* traffic and is recorded as a `refusal` event.\n\n### Loopback-only quick scan\n`python3 -m framework.v2 scan http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ --format json|sarif|html [--strict-evidence]`\n— the export states each finding's **live grounding** (fact / ungrounded / contradicted);\n`--strict-evidence` withholds non-fact findings from the rendered doc but keeps them in\n`--reverifiable-out`.\n\n### Re-verify a report (prove-don't-guess, offline)\n`python3 -m framework.v2 verify <report.json>` re-runs each finding's retained `oracle_context`.\n`python3 -m framework.v2 evidence ...` builds/verifies signed, hash-linked evidence certificates\n(and, with report claims bound in, fails closed when a report sentence has no backing evidence).\n\n### Inspect / audit the event spine\nThe blackboard (`framework/v2/agents/blackboard.py`) is the one append-only, typed, provenance-\nlinked event stream. Replay it with `Blackboard.replay(engagement=..., since_id=...)`.\nCryptographic tamper-evidence: `framework/v2/agents/spine_chain.py`\n(`build_spine_chain` / `sign_spine_head` / `verify_spine_head`).\n\n### Recon / intel, memory, self-improvement\n`python3 -m framework.v2 intel ...` (OSINT into the shared world-model; gated egress),\n`memory ...` (cross-engagement priors — never fabricate a score), `improve ...`\n(authorise-not-apply — it never self-applies a change).\n\n### Read-only operator console\n`python3 -m framework.v2 console` — loopback, read-only, zero-impact operator UI over the run.\n\n## What NOT to do\n- Do not build detection-evasion / identity-rotation / stay-hidden-from-defenders capability —\n  CRUCIBLE is correlatable and authorized by doctrine (constitution §VI).\n- Do not let any learned/critic/LLM signal enter the deterministic oracle/SCE/calibration inputs\n  or promote a finding.\n- Do not attack third parties (payment/IdP/CDN) — test only the operator's integration with them.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"uuid":"bc4955ab-a082-49a6-84b8-26fa34a10f09","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:29:36.300Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

WARDEN autonomy tiers (SIGIL §5). Every tool invocation is classified A0–A3; the gate\n2\t//! decision follows from the tier. FAIL-CLOSED and TOKEN-BASED: the tool name is split into\n3\t//! whole tokens (on `.`/`_`/`-`/`/`/space) and matched against whole-token sets — never a raw\n4\t//! substring, so \"overwrite\" is not \"write\" and \"forget\" is not \"get\". Danger is checked FIRST,\n5\t//! and A0 (auto, un-queued) is reachable ONLY via a positive safe-verb allowlist; anything not\n6\t//! positively classified — including any unknown or dangerous-target tool — is A3.\n7\t\n8\tuse std::fmt;\n9\t\n10\tuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n11\t\n12\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n13\tpub enum Tier {\n14\t    /// Observe / answer — memory queries, screen read, voice reply. Auto.\n15\t    A0,\n16\t    /// Reversible internal act — write a report/brief, draft-branch, raise an alert. Auto + logged.\n17\t    A1,\n18\t    /// External-visible / semi-reversible — send email, calendar write, purchase < cap. Queued.\n19\t    A2,\n20\t    /// Destructive / financial / security — push protected branch, deploy, delete, spend > cap. Explicit.\n21\t    A3,\n22\t}\n23\t\n24\timpl Tier {\n25\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n26\t        match self {\n27\t            Tier::A0 => \"A0\",\n28\t            Tier::A1 => \"A1\",\n29\t            Tier::A2 => \"A2\",\n30\t            Tier::A3 => \"A3\",\n31\t        }\n32\t    }\n33\t}\n34\t\n35\timpl fmt::Display for Tier {\n36\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n37\t        f.write_str(self.as_str())\n38\t    }\n39\t}\n40\t\n41\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n42\tpub enum Decision {\n43\t    Auto,\n44\t    Queued,\n45\t    ExplicitRequired,\n46\t}\n47\t\n48\timpl Decision {\n49\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n50\t        match self {\n51\t            Decision::Auto => \"auto\",\n52\t            Decision::Queued => \"queued\",\n53\t            Decision::ExplicitRequired => \"explicit-required\",\n54\t        }\n55\t    }\n56\t    pub fn may_run(&self) -> bool {\n57\t        matches!(self, Decision::Auto)\n58\t    }\n59\t}\n60\t\n61\t/// A3 — destructive verbs, financial ops, crypto/restore ops, and DANGEROUS TARGETS\n62\t/// (secret/identity/network/prod material is A3 regardless of the verb: `secrets.read`,\n63\t/// `iam.policy.write`, `budget.get`, `vault.read`).\n64\tconst A3_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n65\t    // destructive verbs\n66\t    \"push\", \"deploy\", \"delete\", \"destroy\", \"drop\", \"remove\", \"purge\", \"wipe\", \"truncate\",\n67\t    \"overwrite\", \"erase\", \"format\", \"kill\", \"shutdown\", \"reboot\", \"reset\", \"disable\", \"enable\",\n68\t    \"override\", \"force\", \"sudo\", \"exec\", \"eval\", \"chmod\", \"chown\", \"patch\", \"install\", \"uninstall\",\n69\t    // crypto + restore/rollback (a restore silently reverts current state)\n70\t    \"encrypt\", \"decrypt\", \"restore\", \"revert\", \"rollback\", \"recover\",\n71\t    // financial\n72\t    \"spend\", \"purchase\", \"pay\", \"payment\", \"transaction\", \"transfer\", \"refund\", \"invoice\",\n73\t    \"allocate\", \"budget\", \"release\", \"sign\",\n74\t    // security / identity / infra / secret-store TARGETS (dangerous no matter the verb)\n75\t    \"secret\", \"secrets\", \"credential\", \"credentials\", \"token\", \"tokens\", \"key\", \"keys\", \"iam\",\n76\t    \"policy\", \"firewall\", \"acl\", \"role\", \"grant\", \"revoke\", \"rotate\", \"escalate\", \"infra\",\n77\t    \"prod\", \"production\", \"env\", \"master\", \"root\", \"admin\",\n78\t    \"vault\", \"keyring\", \"keychain\", \"keystore\", \"hsm\",\n79\t];\n80\t\n81\t/// A2 — external-visible / semi-reversible: communication, publishing, and bulk DATA EGRESS\n82\t/// (export/dump of a private store must be human-seen, never auto).\n83\tconst A2_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n84\t    \"send\", \"email\", \"smtp\", \"publish\", \"post\", \"message\", \"outbound\", \"webhook\", \"sms\", \"notify\",\n85\t    \"share\", \"upload\", \"invite\", \"calendar\", \"tweet\", \"dm\", \"export\", \"dump\", \"download\", \"sync\",\n86\t];\n87\t\n88\t/// A1 — reversible internal writes (drafts, notes, memory writes, non-push commits). NOTE:\n89\t/// \"snapshot\" is intentionally NOT here — a snapshot RESTORE is destructive (caught by A3\n90\t/// \"restore\"), and snapshot-create alone falls to fail-closed A3 rather than risk auto-run.\n91\tconst A1_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n92\t    \"write\", \"note\", \"brief\", \"report\", \"draft\", \"alert\", \"consolidate\", \"commit\", \"branch\",\n93\t    \"annotate\", \"tag\", \"label\",\n94\t];\n95\t\n96\t/// A0 — POSITIVE allowlist of known-safe observe/answer VERBS only (NO target nouns — a target\n97\t/// noun here would let e.g. `memory.encrypt` auto-run). A tool reaches A0 only by a read-verb\n98\t/// here, or an exact name in `A0_TOOLS`; absence of danger alone is NOT sufficient → fail-closed A3.\n99\tconst A0_VERBS: &[&str] = &[\n100\t    \"read\", \"search\", \"query\", \"get\", \"list\", \"status\", \"recall\", \"observe\", \"answer\",\n101\t    \"view\", \"show\", \"find\", \"frame\", \"peek\", \"describe\", \"inspect\", \"lookup\",\n102\t];\n103\t\n104\t/// A0 — exact-name allowlist for the known read-only memory tools whose names are not verb-clean\n105\t/// (`graph.entity`, `episodic.range`, `threads.open`, `commitments.due`, `contradictions.pending`,\n106\t/// `ingest.status`). Matched on the whole lowercased tool name.\n107\tconst A0_TOOLS: &[&str] = &[\n108\t    \"memory.search\", \"graph.query\", \"graph.entity\", \"episodic.range\", \"ingest.status\",\n109\t    \"threads.open\", \"commitments.due\", \"contradictions.pending\",\n110\t];\n111\t\n112\t/// Split a tool name into whole tokens on `.`/`_`/`-`/`/` and whitespace, lowercased.\n113\tfn tokens(tool: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n114\t    tool.split(|c: char| c == '.' || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '/' || c.is_whitespace())\n115\t        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n116\t        .map(|s| s.to_ascii_lowercase())\n117\t        .collect()\n118\t}\n119\t\n120\t/// Classify a tool name into a tier. Danger FIRST, then A2, A1; A0 only via a positive safe-verb\n121\t/// or an exact safe-tool name; everything else (unknown / not-positively-safe / empty) → A3.\n122\tpub fn classify(tool: &str) -> Tier {\n123\t    let full = tool.to_ascii_lowercase();\n124\t    let tk = tokens(tool);\n125\t    if tk.is_empty() {\n126\t        return Tier::A3;\n127\t    }\n128\t    let has = |set: &[&str]| tk.iter().any(|t| set.contains(&t.as_str()));\n129\t    if has(A3_TOKENS) {\n130\t        return Tier::A3;\n131\t    }\n132\t    if has(A2_TOKENS) {\n133\t        return Tier::A2;\n134\t    }\n135\t    if has(A1_TOKENS) {\n136\t        return Tier::A1;\n137\t    }\n138\t    if A0_TOOLS.contains(&full.as_str()) || has(A0_VERBS) {\n139\t        return Tier::A0;\n140\t    }\n141\t    Tier::A3 // not positively classified → fail-closed to the most-gated tier\n142\t}\n143\t\n144\tpub fn gate(tier: Tier) -> Decision {\n145\t    match tier {\n146\t        Tier::A0 | Tier::A1 => Decision::Auto,\n147\t        Tier::A2 => Decision::Queued,\n148\t        Tier::A3 => Decision::ExplicitRequired,\n149\t    }\n150\t}\n151\t\n152\t#[cfg(test)]\n153\tmod tests {\n154\t    use super::*;\n155\t\n156\t    #[test]\n157\t    fn classification_matches_spec_examples() {\n158\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.search\"), Tier::A0);\n159\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"graph.query\"), Tier::A0);\n160\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.write\"), Tier::A1);\n161\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"brief.compose\"), Tier::A1);\n162\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"email.send\"), Tier::A2);\n163\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"calendar.write\"), Tier::A2); // \"calendar\" (A2) beats \"write\" (A1)\n164\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"git.push\"), Tier::A3);\n165\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"deploy.prod\"), Tier::A3);\n166\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"data.delete\"), Tier::A3);\n167\t    }\n168\t\n169\t    #[test]\n170\t    fn unknown_and_empty_are_fail_closed_a3() {\n171\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"something.unclassified\"), Tier::A3);\n172\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"\"), Tier::A3);\n173\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"weird\"), Tier::A3);\n174\t        assert_eq!(gate(classify(\"something.unclassified\")), Decision::ExplicitRequired);\n175\t    }\n176\t\n177\t    #[test]\n178\t    fn substring_collisions_do_not_lower_the_tier() {\n179\t        // the exact review findings: a dangerous op must NOT ride a benign substring down a tier\n180\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"config.overwrite\"), Tier::A3, \"overwrite != write\");\n181\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"db.overwrite\"), Tier::A3);\n182\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"files.forget\"), Tier::A3, \"forget != get; fail-closed\");\n183\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"budget.override\"), Tier::A3, \"financial + override\");\n184\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"budget.get\"), Tier::A3, \"financial target is A3 regardless of verb\");\n185\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"iam.policy.write\"), Tier::A3, \"identity write is A3, not A1\");\n186\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"firewall.rule.write\"), Tier::A3);\n187\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"transaction.sign\"), Tier::A3, \"financial signing is A3, not A1\");\n188\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"secrets.read\"), Tier::A3, \"secret read is A3, not A0\");\n189\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"credentials.get\"), Tier::A3);\n190\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"account.disable\"), Tier::A3);\n191\t    }\n192\t\n193\t    #[test]\n194\t    fn dangerous_ops_on_safe_targets_do_not_auto_run() {\n195\t        // the CRITICAL re-check finding: a target noun must NOT grant A0 to a dangerous verb\n196\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.encrypt\"), Tier::A3, \"ransomware-shaped op must NOT be A0\");\n197\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"graph.destroy\"), Tier::A3);\n198\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"entity.merge\"), Tier::A3, \"irreversible rewrite → fail-closed, not A0\");\n199\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.export\"), Tier::A2, \"full-store egress must be queued, not auto\");\n200\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.dump\"), Tier::A2);\n201\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"snapshot.restore\"), Tier::A3, \"a restore reverts state → A3\");\n202\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"vault.read\"), Tier::A3, \"secret-store read is A3 regardless of verb\");\n203\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"keyring.get\"), Tier::A3);\n204\t    }\n205\t\n206\t assert_eq!(classify(\"delete.and.list\"), Tier::A3);\n220\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"search.and.deploy\"), Tier::A3);\n221\t    }\n222\t\n223\t    #[test]\n224\t    fn gates_are_correct() {\n225\t WARDEN — the authorization kernel (SIGIL §5). The single choke point every tool invocation\n2\t//! crosses: classify the tool into a tier, derive the fail-closed gate decision, and (after the\n3\t//! caller executes-or-blocks) append a signed, chained action-log record. WARDEN never executes\n4\t//! tools itself; it decides and it records.\n5\t\n6\tuse std::io;\n7\tuse std::path::Path;\n8\t\n9\tuse crate::actionlog::{ActionLog, ActionRecord};\n10\tuse crate::crypto::WardenKey;\n11\tuse crate::registry::Registry;\n12\tuse crate::tiers::{gate, Decision, Tier};\n13\t\n14\tpub struct Warden {\n15\t    log: ActionLog,\n16\t    key: WardenKey,\n17\t    registry: Registry,\n18\t}\n19\t\n20\tpub struct Verdict {\n21\t    pub tier: Tier,\n22\t    pub decision: Decision,\n23\t}\n24\t\n25\timpl Warden {\n26\t    /// Open (or initialize) WARDEN under `dir`: the signing key lives in `dir/keys`, the action\n27\t    /// log at `dir/actionlog.jsonl`.\n28\t    pub fn open(dir: &Path) -> io::Result<Self> {\n29\t        let key = WardenKey::load_or_create(&dir.join(\"keys\"))?;\n30\t        let log = ActionLog::new(dir.join(\"actionlog.jsonl\"));\n31\t        let registry = Registry::load(&dir.join(\"tools.json\"));\n32\t        Ok(Warden { log, key, registry })\n33\t    }\n34\t\n35\t    /// Classify + derive the gate decision (pure — no logging, no side effects). The tier is the\n36\t    /// raise-only registry result (an explicit pin can only make a tool MORE gated than inferred).\n37\t    pub fn decide(&self, tool: &str) -> Verdict {\n38\t        let tier = self.registry.tier(tool);\n39\t        Verdict { tier, decision: gate(tier) }\n40\t    }\n41\t\n42\t    /// Append a signed action-log record for a completed (or blocked) invocation.\n43\t    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n44\t    pub fn record(\n45\t        &self,\n46\t        agent: &str,\n47\t        tool: &str,\n48\t        args_hash: &str,\n49\t        verdict: &Verdict,\n50\t        approver: &str,\n51\t        result_hash: &str,\n52\t        ts_epoch: u64,\n53\t    ) -> io::Result<ActionRecord> {\n54\t        self.log.append(\n55\t            &self.key, agent, tool, args_hash,\n56\t            verdict.tier.as_str(), verdict.decision.as_str(),\n57\t            approver, result_hash, ts_epoch,\n58\t        )\n59\t    }\n60\t\n61\t    pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<usize, String> {\n62\t        self.log.verify(&self.key.public_hex())\n63\t    }\n64\t\n65\t    pub fn records(&self) -> io::Result<Vec<ActionRecord>> {\n66\t        self.log.records()\n67\t    }\n68\t\n69\t    /// The on-disk signed head as (count, head_hash) — for the anti-rollback anchor.\n70\t    pub fn head(&self) -> io::Result<Option<(u64, String)>> {\n71\t        self.log.head()\n72\t    }\n73\t\n74\t    pub fn public_hex(&self) -> String {\n75\t        self.key.public_hex()\n76\t    }\n77\t\n78\t    /// Sign a message with the WARDEN key (hex) — used to authenticate anchor-set to the spine.\n79\t    pub fn sign_hex(&self, msg: &[u8]) -> String {\n80\t        self.key.sign_hex(msg)\n81\t    }\n82\t}\n83\t\n84\t#[cfg(test)]\n85\tmod tests {\n86\t    use super::*;\n87\t    use crate::crypto::sha256_hex;\n88\t\n89\t    fn tmp_dir() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n90\t        let mut p = std::env::temp_dir();\n91\t        p.push(format!(\"sigil-warden-{}\", sha256_hex(format!(\"{:?}\", std::thread::current().id()).as_bytes())));\n92\t        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&p);\n93\t        p\n94\t    }\n95\t\n96\t    #[test]\n97\t    fn a0_a1_auto_run_a2_a3_blocked() {\n98\t        let w = Warden::open(&tmp_dir()).unwrap();\n99\t        assert!(w.decide(\"memory.search\").decision.may_run(), \"A0 must auto-run\");\n100\t        assert!(w.decide(\"memory.write\").decision.may_run(), \"A1 must auto-run\");\n101\t        assert!(!w.decide(\"email.send\").decision.may_run(), \"A2 must NOT auto-run\");\n102\t        assert!(!w.decide(\"git.push\").decision.may_run(), \"A3 must NOT auto-run\");\n103\t        assert!(!w.decide(\"unknown.thing\").decision.may_run(), \"unknown must fail closed\");\n104\t    }\n105\t\n106\t    #[test]\n107\t    fn recorded_actions_verify_and_survive_reopen() {\n108\t        let dir = tmp_dir();\n109\t        {\n110\t            let w = Warden::open(&dir).unwrap();\n111\t            let v = w.decide(\"memory.search\");\n112\t            w.record(\"KERNEL\", \"memory.search\", \"b3:aa\", &v, \"auto\", \"b3:res\", 1000).unwrap();\n113\t        }\n114\t        // reopen (loads the same persisted key) and append + verify\n115\t        let w2 = Warden::open(&dir).unwrap();\n116\t        let v = w2.decide(\"email.send\");\n117\t        w2.record(\"ENVOY\", \"email.send\", \"b3:bb\", &v, \"none\", \"blocked:queued\", 1001).unwrap();\n118\t        assert_eq!(w2.verify().unwrap(), 2, \"the whole log must verify under the persisted key\");\n119\t    }\n120\t}\n121\t"}]},"uuid":"2176649c-7ee0-4ae1-9072-923cf027cd95","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:30:15.874Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"61d6639b-68b5-4ccc-a548-dd9444dbc41f","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Per-tool tier registry (Phase 1.1) — the auditable complement to name-inference. A pin makes\n2\t//! classification EXPLICIT for a named tool. Crucially it is **RAISE-ONLY**: the effective tier\n3\t//! is `max(pin, inferred)`, so the override file (`~/.sigil/warden/tools.json`, plain text a\n4\t//! file-write attacker could edit) can only ever make a tool MORE gated, never less — it can\n5\t//! never downgrade `git.push` to auto. Legitimate de-escalation is intentionally NOT available\n6\t//! via an unsigned file (that would need a signed mechanism; a future addition).\n7\t\n8\tuse std::collections::HashMap;\n9\tuse std::path::Path;\n10\t\n11\tuse crate::tiers::{classify, Tier};\n12\t\n13\tpub struct Registry {\n14\t    pins: HashMap<String, Tier>,\n15\t}\n16\t\n17\tfn parse_tier(s: &str) -> Option<Tier> {\n18\t    match s.trim().to_ascii_uppercase().as_str() {\n19\t        \"A0\" => Some(Tier::A0),\n20\t        \"A1\" => Some(Tier::A1),\n21\t        \"A2\" => Some(Tier::A2),\n22\t        \"A3\" => Some(Tier::A3),\n23\t        _ => None,\n24\t    }\n25\t}\n26\t\n27\timpl Registry {\n28\t    pub fn empty() -> Self {\n29\t        Registry { pins: HashMap::new() }\n30\t    }\n31\t\n32\t    /// Load raise-only pins from a JSON object `{ \"tool.name\": \"A2\", ... }`. Unreadable/absent\n33\t    /// file or malformed entries are ignored (the inference engine still governs). Never fails.\n34\t    pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Self {\n35\t        let mut r = Registry::empty();\n36\t        if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(path) {\n37\t            if let Ok(map) = serde_json::from_str::<HashMap<String, String>>(&text) {\n38\t                for (tool, tier_s) in map {\n39\t                    if let Some(t) = parse_tier(&tier_s) {\n40\t                        // case-colliding keys resolve to the HIGHER tier (deterministic +\n41\t                        // raise-only-consistent), never last-writer-wins by hash order.\n42\t                        let key = tool.to_ascii_lowercase();\n43\t                        let eff = r.pins.get(&key).map_or(t, |&e| e.max(t));\n44\t                        r.pins.insert(key, eff);\n45\t                    }\n46\t                }\n47\t            }\n48\t        }\n49\t        r\n50\t    }\n51\t\n52\t    /// The effective tier: `max(pin, inferred)`. A pin can only RAISE (never lower) the\n53\t    /// token-inference result, so the override file is not a downgrade attack surface.\n54\t    pub fn tier(&self, tool: &str) -> Tier {\n55\t        let inferred = classify(tool);\n56\t        match self.pins.get(&tool.to_ascii_lowercase()) {\n57\t            Some(&pinned) => pinned.max(inferred),\n58\t            None => inferred,\n59\t        }\n60\t    }\n61\t}\n62\t\n63\t#[cfg(test)]\n64\tmod tests {\n65\t    use super::*;\n66\t\n67\t    #[test]\n68\t    fn a_pin_can_raise_but_never_lower() {\n69\t        let mut r = Registry::empty();\n70\t        r.pins.insert(\"custom.report\".into(), Tier::A3); // owner marks a report tool extra-sensitive\n71\t        assert_eq!(r.tier(\"custom.report\"), Tier::A3, \"pin raises A1→A3\");\n72\t\n73\t        // an ATTACKER pinning a dangerous tool to A0 must NOT downgrade it\n74\t        r.pins.insert(\"git.push\".into(), Tier::A0);\n75\t        assert_eq!(r.tier(\"git.push\"), Tier::A3, \"raise-only: a pin can never lower git.push below its inferred A3\");\n76\t\n77\t        // a pin at/below the inferred tier is a no-op\n78\t        r.pins.insert(\"memory.search\".into(), Tier::A0);\n79\t        assert_eq!(r.tier(\"memory.search\"), Tier::A0);\n80\t    }\n81\t\n82\t    #[test]\n83\t    fn case_colliding_pins_resolve_to_the_higher_tier_deterministically() {\n84\t        let mut p = std::env::temp_dir();\n85\t        p.push(format!(\"sigil-reg-{}.json\", std::process::id()));\n86\t        // both keys lowercase to \"note.write\"; last-writer-wins would be nondeterministic\n87\t        std::fs::write(&p, r#\"{\"Note.Write\":\"A2\",\"note.write\":\"A1\"}\"#).unwrap();\n88\t        let r = Registry::load(&p);\n89\t        assert_eq!(r.tier(\"note.write\"), Tier::A2, \"collision → max pin (A2), raised from inferred A1\");\n90\t        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);\n91\t    }\n92\t\n93\t    #[test]\n94\t    fn unregistered_tools_fall_through_to_inference() {\n95\t        let r = Registry::empty();\n96\t        assert_eq!(r.tier(\"memory.search\"), Tier::A0);\n97\t        assert_eq!(r.tier(\"memory.encrypt\"), Tier::A3);\n98\t        assert_eq!(r.tier(\"totally.unknown\"), Tier::A3); // fail-closed inference\n99\t    }\n100\t}\n101\t"}]},"uuid":"bdfdadbd-6b05-4085-9026-699eb600096b","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:30:16.077Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"fe5f39bd-8e10-4b7b-ac38-17a905ff0290","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"53f155c1-d008-4191-b253-584ef16e22df","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"ffbb8a8a-4bb8-4c99-a79e-9ed4dd97a041","agentId":"aa30cb33429fa06f7","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014FkJ8MrMwagdYtR62EyUE1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"KernelClassifier (Phase 7, P0.1) — the Python↔Rust WARDEN bridge. The authoritative danger\n2\tclassifier is Rust `kernel/src/tiers.rs::classify` (token-based, danger-first, fail-closed to A3),\n3\tcomposed with the raise-only registry pins in `Warden::decide`. Python's `Governor` otherwise\n4\tTRUSTS a Proposal's declared tier; this bridge lets the mesh DERIVE a tool's tier from that\n5\tfail-closed oracle instead of self-declaring it — so an Operator step or a Vision egress hop is\n6\ttiered by the same code that enforces at the kernel.\n7\t\n8\tConsulting the kernel is a pure A0 observation (`sigil-kernel classify` writes NO action-log\n9\trecord). Any failure — missing binary, timeout, non-zero exit, unparseable output, or an unknown\n10\ttier string — resolves to **A3** (fail-closed to the most-gated tier), mirroring the Rust\n11\tclassifier's own posture: never let a bridge error silently downgrade a dangerous tool.\"\"\"\n12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n13\t\n14\timport json\n15\timport subprocess\n16\t\n17\tfrom ..voice.dispatch import _default_bin  # reuse the exact kernel-binary resolution\n18\tfrom .base import Tier\n19\t\n20\t_TIER = {\"A0\": Tier.A0, \"A1\": Tier.A1, \"A2\": Tier.A2, \"A3\": Tier.A3}\n21\t\n22\t\n23\tclass KernelClassifier:\n24\t    def __init__(self, kernel_bin: str | None = None, timeout: int = 15):\n25\t        self.kernel_bin = kernel_bin or _default_bin()\n26\t        self.timeout = timeout\n27\t\n28\t    def classify(self, tool: str) -> Tier:\n29\t        \"\"\"Return the WARDEN tier for `tool`. Fail-closed to A3 on ANY error/ambiguity.\"\"\"\n30\t        if not tool or not tool.strip():\n31\t            return Tier.A3\n32\t        try:\n33\t            proc = subprocess.run([self.kernel_bin, \"classify\", tool, \"--json\"],\n34\t                                  capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=self.timeout)\n35\t        except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError):\n36\t            return Tier.A3\n37\t        if proc.returncode != 0:\n38\t            return Tier.A3\n39\t        try:\n40\t            data = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])\n41\t            return _TIER.get(str(data.get(\"tier\")), Tier.A3)\n42\t        except (ValueError, IndexError, KeyError, TypeError):\n43\t            return Tier.A3\n44\t"}]},"uuid":"39cf9bac-b343-41b2-99cb-a16bb152a549","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:30:22.943Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"53f155c1-d008-4191-b253-584ef16e22df","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

It performs the two per-atom checks the store's `verify()` does for\n4\tthe whole log, on a single record:\n5\t\n6\t  1. BINDING — the record's content still hashes to its stored `cert_digest` (catches a silent\n7\t     payload edit).\n8\t  2. DERIVATION — `entry_hash` is correctly derived from (seq, prev_hash, cert_digest) (catches an\n9\t     entry-field tamper).\n10\t\n11\tCross-record LINKAGE (prev_hash == the predecessor's entry_hash) needs the predecessor and is done\n12\tby `SpineTailer` as records stream. Reuses `reuse.digest_payload` and the canonical `_entry_hash`\n13\tfrom `reuse.chain` verbatim — never a re-implementation that could drift from the enforced path.\"\"\"\n14\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n15\t\n16\tfrom ..reuse import digest_payload\n17\tfrom ..reuse.chain import _entry_hash\n18\t\n19\t\n20\tdef verify_record(record) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n21\t    \"\"\"(ok, reason) for a single SpineRecord — binding + entry-hash derivation. Fail-closed.\"\"\"\n22\t    content = {\n23\t        \"scope\": record.scope, \"kind\": record.kind, \"source\": record.source, \"actor\": record.actor,\n24\t        \"payload\": record.payload, \"parent_id\": record.parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": record.supersedes_id,\n25\t    }\n26\t    if digest_payload(content) != record.cert_digest:\n27\t        return False, f\"binding break at seq {record.seq}: payload does not match cert_digest (record tampered)\"\n28\t    if _entry_hash(record.seq, record.prev_hash, record.cert_digest) != record.entry_hash:\n29\t        return False, f\"entry_hash mismatch at seq {record.seq}: derivation broken (entry tampered)\"\n30\t    return True, f\"seq {record.seq} binds and derives cleanly\"\n31\t"}]},"uuid":"08192373-446d-4985-9ce9-c74a2b0418cc","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:30:23.427Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0f28aade-4f2f-425d-972c-55555f30a3b9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"217ff983-aa52-4594-b324-8b975e387b6e","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"ffbb8a8a-4bb8-4c99-a79e-9ed4dd97a041","agentId":"aa30cb33429fa06f7","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019WZdG3ukuSUq5Mdk17UBmL","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"SpineTailer (Phase 7, P0.2) — an integrity-verifying live tail over the append-only, poll-only\n2\tspine. The spine has no push/inotify; `iter_records(since_seq=N)` is the cursor primitive. This\n3\tturns it into an event source that PROVES each atom before emitting it: on each `poll()` it reads\n4\tthe records after its cursor and, for every one, checks (a) per-atom binding+derivation\n5\t(`verify_record`) and (b) cross-record LINKAGE (this record's `prev_hash` == the last emitted\n6\trecord's `entry_hash`). A tamper, rewind, or fork is caught on the LIVE edge — the offending event\n7\tis emitted flagged `integrity_ok=False` (so a consumer badges it \"integrity broken\" and NEVER shows\n8\tit as truth), never silently dropped and never fabricated into a clean gap.\n9\t\n10\tOne primitive, two consumers: the UI SSE feed and the mobile push notifier both drive `poll()` on a\n11\ttick and fan the events out via `Broadcaster` (bounded per-subscriber queues; on overflow it drops\n12\toldest and raises a `lagged` flag so the consumer resyncs from the cursor rather than believing it\n13\tsaw everything).\"\"\"\n14\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n15\t\n16\tfrom collections import deque\n17\tfrom typing import Optional\n18\t\n19\tfrom ..reuse.chain import _GENESIS_PREV\n20\tfrom .store import SpineStore\n21\tfrom .verify import verify_record\n22\t\n23\t\n24\tdef _shape(record, *, integrity_ok: bool, integrity_reason: str) -> dict:\n25\t    \"\"\"The cited atom shape emitted to consumers — same fields the MCP tools serve, plus the live\n26\t    integrity verdict. `text` is the record's best-effort display text (never fabricated).\"\"\"\n27\t    return {\n28\t        \"seq\": record.seq, \"kind\": record.kind, \"source\": record.source, \"actor\": record.actor,\n29\t        \"ts\": record.ts, \"entry_hash\": record.entry_hash, \"text\": record.text(),\n30\t        \"integrity_ok\": integrity_ok, \"integrity_reason\": integrity_reason,\n31\t    }\n32\t\n33\t\n34\tclass SpineTailer:\n35\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, since_seq: int = -1):\n36\t        \"\"\"Emit records with seq > `since_seq`. Use `since_seq = store.next_seq - 1` for live-only\n37\t        (no backlog), or a resume cursor to catch up. `_last_hash` seeds the linkage check: for a\n38\t        from-genesis tail it is the genesis marker; for a resume it is seeded from the record AT the\n39\t        cursor so the first new record's `prev_hash` is checked against the real predecessor.\"\"\"\n40\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n41\t        self.cursor = since_seq\n42\t        if since_seq < 0:\n43\t            self._last_hash = _GENESIS_PREV\n44\t        else:\n45\t            anchor = self.store.get(since_seq)\n46\t            self._last_hash = anchor.entry_hash if anchor else _GENESIS_PREV\n47\t\n48\t    def poll(self) -> list[dict]:\n49\t        \"\"\"Return newly-appended records (seq > cursor), each verified. Advances the cursor. On an\n50\t        integrity failure the event is emitted flagged (not dropped); the cursor still advances so\n51\t        the feed never re-emits or stalls, and `_last_hash` follows the on-disk chain.\"\"\"\n52\t        out: list[dict] = []\n53\t        for r in self.store.iter_records(since_seq=self.cursor):\n54\t            atom_ok, atom_reason = verify_record(r)\n55\t            if r.prev_hash != self._last_hash:\n56\t                ok, reason = False, (f\"linkage break at seq {r.seq}: prev_hash != last emitted \"\n57\t                                     f\"entry_hash (rewind/fork/gap)\")\n58\t            else:\n59\t                ok, reason = atom_ok, atom_reason\n60\t            out.append(_shape(r, integrity_ok=ok, integrity_reason=reason))\n61\t            self.cursor = r.seq\n62\t            self._last_hash = r.entry_hash\n63\t        return out\n64\t\n65\t\n66\tclass Broadcaster:\n67\t    \"\"\"Fan-out of tail events to N subscribers with bounded per-subscriber queues. On overflow the\n68\t    oldest events are dropped and the subscriber is marked `lagged` so it resyncs from the cursor\n69\t    (never a fabricated 'you saw everything').\"\"\"\n70\t    def __init__(self, maxlen: int = 512):\n71\t        self.maxlen = maxlen\n72\t        self._subs: dict[int, deque] = {}\n73\t        self._lagged: dict[int, bool] = {}\n74\t        self._next_id = 0\n75\t\n76\t    def subscribe(self) -> int:\n77\t        sid = self._next_id\n78\t        self._next_id += 1\n79\t        self._subs[sid] = deque(maxlen=self.maxlen)\n80\t        self._lagged[sid] = False\n81\t        return sid\n82\t\n83\t    def unsubscribe(self, sid: int) -> None:\n84\t        self._subs.pop(sid, None)\n85\t        self._lagged.pop(sid, None)\n86\t\n87\t    def publish(self, events: list[dict]) -> None:\n88\t        for sid, q in self._subs.items():\n89\t            for ev in events:\n90\t                if len(q) == self.maxlen:        # would drop the oldest → the subscriber lagged\n91\t                    self._lagged[sid] = True\n92\t                q.append(ev)\n93\t\n94\t    def drain(self, sid: int) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:\n95\t        \"\"\"Return (events, lagged) and clear both. `lagged=True` tells the consumer to resync.\"\"\"\n96\t        q = self._subs.get(sid)\n97\t        if q is None:\n98\t            return [], False\n99\t        events = list(q)\n100\t        q.clear()\n101\t        lagged = self._lagged.get(sid, False)\n102\t        self._lagged[sid] = False\n103\t        return events, lagged\n104\t"}]},"uuid":"35dad8a1-3864-48a5-9dc8-fe0a48548203","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:30:23.893Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"217ff983-aa52-4594-b324-8b975e387b6e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

The\n5\t`cert_digest` is over the record's CONTENT only (scope/kind/source/actor/payload/\n6\tparent/supersedes) — NOT the wallclock `ts` — so the chain is replay-stable. Appends\n7\tare O(1): read the last line's entry, `append_entry`, write.\n8\t\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\timport json\n12\timport os\n13\tfrom pathlib import Path\n14\tfrom typing import Any, Iterator\n15\t\n16\tfrom ..config import SCOPE, SPINE_PATH\n17\tfrom ..reuse import ChainEntry, append_entry, build_chain, digest_payload, verify_chain\n18\tfrom .models import SpineRecord, now_iso\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tdef _last_nonempty_line(path: Path) -> str | None:\n22\t    \"\"\"Read the last non-empty line without loading the file (seek-from-end).\"\"\"\n23\t    with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n24\t        f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)\n25\t        end = f.tell()\n26\t        if end == 0:\n27\t            return None\n28\t        buf = b\"\"\n29\t        pos = end\n30\t        while pos > 0:\n31\t            step = min(8192, pos)\n32\t            pos -= step\n33\t            f.seek(pos)\n34\t            buf = f.read(step) + buf\n35\t            lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n36\t            if lines and (pos == 0 or buf.count(b\"\\n\") >= 2):\n37\t                return lines[-1].decode(\"utf-8\")\n38\t        lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n39\t        return lines[-1].decode(\"utf-8\") if lines else None\n40\t\n41\t\n42\tclass SpineStore:\n43\t    def __init__(self, path: Path | str = SPINE_PATH) -> None:\n44\t        self.path = Path(path)\n45\t        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n46\t        self._last: ChainEntry | None = self._read_last_entry()\n47\t\n48\t    # --- write --------------------------------------------------------------------\n49\t    def append(\n50\t        self, *, kind: str, source: str, actor: str, payload: dict[str, Any],\n51\t        parent_id: int | None = None, supersedes_id: int | None = None,\n52\t        ts: str | None = None,\n53\t    ) -> int:\n54\t        content = {\n55\t            \"scope\": SCOPE, \"kind\": kind, \"source\": source, \"actor\": actor,\n56\t            \"payload\": payload, \"parent_id\": parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": supersedes_id,\n57\t        }\n58\t        cert_digest = digest_payload(content)  # wallclock-free\n59\t        entry = append_entry([self._last], cert_digest) if self._last else build_chain([cert_digest])[0]\n60\t        record = {\n61\t            \"seq\": entry.seq, **content, \"ts\": ts or now_iso(),\n62\t            \"cert_digest\": cert_digest, \"prev_hash\": entry.prev_hash, \"entry_hash\": entry.entry_hash,\n63\t        }\n64\t        with self.path.open(\"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n65\t            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n66\t        self._last = entry\n67\t        return entry.seq\n68\t\n69\t    # Behaviour is byte-identical.\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n8\t\n9\timport hashlib\n10\timport json\n11\tfrom typing import Any, Final\n12\t\n13\t# Never change without a schema bump + migration (invalidates all existing signatures).\n14\t_EVIDENCE_DOMAIN: Final[bytes] = b\"crucible-evidence-v1\\x00\"\n15\t\n16\t\n17\tdef canonical_json(payload: Any) -> bytes:\n18\t    \"\"\"Deterministic UTF-8 JSON: sorted keys (recursive), compact separators.\"\"\"\n19\t    return json.dumps(\n20\t        payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"), ensure_ascii=False,\n21\t    ).encode(\"utf-8\")\n22\t\n23\t\n24\tdef sha256_hex(data: bytes) -> str:\n25\t    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()\n26\t\n27\t\n28\tdef digest_payload(payload: Any) -> str:\n29\t    \"\"\"sha256 of a JSON-serialisable payload in canonical form.\"\"\"\n30\t    return sha256_hex(canonical_json(payload))\n31\t\n32\t\n33\tdef evidence_signing_bytes(certificate_payload: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:\n34\t    \"\"\"The exact bytes signed/verified (canonical JSON under the domain tag).\"\"\"\n35\t    return _EVIDENCE_DOMAIN + canonical_json(certificate_payload)\n36\t"}]},"uuid":"14c5f77e-e0a1-40fb-8fbc-30a4aa5e9478","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:33:15.626Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"348a506b-1926-4fe0-8d86-19ee8d25e6ef","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

description=\"base64(64-byte Ed25519 signature).\")\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tclass AuthorizerKey(BaseModel):\n22\t    \"\"\"One authoriser's Ed25519 public key (base64 of the 32-byte raw pubkey).\"\"\"\n23\t = Field(ge=1, description=\"m in m-of-n. 1 also covers FROST group keys.\")\n34\t    authorizers: list[AuthorizerKey] = Field(min_length=1)\n35\t\n36\t    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n37\t    def {"parentUuid":"59bad103-4d8d-4634-8452-ed4cf267f476","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"ffbb8a8a-4bb8-4c99-a79e-9ed4dd97a041","agentId":"aa30cb33429fa06f7","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HXvkbHqAHR4tnuEMsLbyEm","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"The SIGIL agent mesh framework (SIGIL §4/§5). Each agent has a MANDATE and an AUTONOMY\n2\tCEILING (A0–A3); everything it does is a `Proposal` carrying a tier. Proposals at or below the\n3\tauto bar (A1) and at or below the agent's ceiling are AUTO-APPLIED (written to the spine);\n4\tanything higher is QUEUED as a pending record a human must approve — never auto-executed.\n5\t\n6\tThe doctrine is enforced STRUCTURALLY, not by discipline: an agent literally cannot take an\n7\texternal-effect action, because no agent has a send/deploy/spend code path. ENVOY, in\n8\tparticular, drafts only — its ceiling is A2 and there is no method that transmits. Agent output\n9\tis provenance-linked spine records, so a brief or a draft is auditable back to what produced it.\"\"\"\n10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n11\t\n12\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n13\tfrom enum import IntEnum\n14\tfrom typing import List, Optional\n15\t\n16\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n17\t\n18\tAGENTS_SOURCE = \"agent\"\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tclass Tier(IntEnum):\n22\t    \"\"\"Mirror of the WARDEN tiers (SIGIL §5), ordered so `<=` compares autonomy.\"\"\"\n23\t    A0 = 0   # observe / answer\n24\t    A1 = 1   # reversible internal act (write a report/brief/event) — the AUTO bar\n25\t    A2 = 2   # external-visible / semi-reversible (send, calendar write) — QUEUED\n26\t    A3 = 3   # destructive / financial / security — explicit, never auto\n27\t\n28\t    def label(self) -> str:\n29\t        return self.name\n30\t\n31\t\n32\tAUTO_BAR = Tier.A1  # A0/A1 auto-apply; A2/A3 queue for human approval\n33\t\n34\t\n35\t@dataclass\n36\tclass Proposal:\n37\t    \"\"\"One thing an agent wants to do: emit a record (auto) or take a gated action (queued).\"\"\"\n38\t    kind: str                       # spine record kind (event/finding/brief/interaction/draft/...)\n39\t    payload: dict\n40\t    tier: Tier = Tier.A1\n41\t    parent_id: Optional[int] = None\n42\t    supersedes_id: Optional[int] = None   # this record supersedes an earlier one (e.g. a resolution)\n43\t\n44\t\n45\t@dataclass\n46\tclass AgentResult:\n47\t    agent: str\n48\t    applied: List[int] = field(default_factory=list)     # seqs written (auto)\n49\t    queued: List[dict] = field(default_factory=list)      # proposals held for approval\n50\t    notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n51\t\n52\t\n53\tclass Agent:\n54\t    \"\"\"Base agent. Subclasses implement `run()`; the base routes every Proposal through the GOVERNOR\n55\t    (SIGIL §5: kill switch, budgets, promotion — Phase 6) and records the outcome on the spine.\n56\t    Backward compatible: with no kill/cap/promotion the governor reproduces the original gate.\"\"\"\n57\t    name: str = \"AGENT\"\n58\t    mandate: str = \"\"\n59\t    ceiling: Tier = Tier.A1\n60\t\n61\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, governor=None):\n62\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n63\t        if governor is None:\n64\t            from ..governor import Governor\n65\t            governor = Governor(self.store)\n66\t        self.governor = governor\n67\t\n68\t    def run(self) -> AgentResult:\n69\t        raise NotImplementedError\n70\t\n71\t    def _dispatch(self, proposals: List[Proposal]) -> AgentResult:\n72\t        from ..governor import Outcome\n73\t        res = AgentResult(agent=self.name)\n74\t        for p in proposals:\n75\t            effective = max(p.tier, Tier.A0)\n76\t            # promotion scope = the RECORD KIND (the real action written), not a self-asserted label:\n77\t            # a promotion is \"this agent may auto-approve A2 records of this kind\" (red-pen RP-3).\n78\t            decision = self.governor.decide(agent=self.name, tier=effective,\n79\t                                            ceiling=self.ceiling, scope=p.kind)\n80\t            common = {**p.payload, \"agent\": self.name, \"tier\": effective.label(),\n81\t                      \"governor\": decision.reason}\n82\t            if decision.outcome == Outcome.AUTO:\n83\t                seq = self.store.append(kind=p.kind, source=AGENTS_SOURCE, actor=self.name,\n84\t                                        payload={**common, \"decision\": \"auto\"},\n85\t                                        parent_id=p.parent_id, supersedes_id=p.supersedes_id)\n86\t                res.applied.append(seq)\n87\t            elif decision.outcome == Outcome.QUEUE:\n88\t                seq = self.store.append(kind=p.kind, source=AGENTS_SOURCE, actor=self.name,\n89\t                                        payload={**common, \"decision\": \"queued\", \"status\": \"awaiting-approval\"},\n90\t                                        parent_id=p.parent_id, supersedes_id=p.supersedes_id)\n91\t                res.queued.append({\"seq\": seq, \"kind\": p.kind, \"tier\": effective.label(),\n92\t                                   \"subject\": p.payload.get(\"subject\") or p.payload.get(\"to\")})\n93\t            else:  # DENY — kill switch or budget; record the refusal, take no action\n94\t                self.store.append(kind=\"refusal\", source=AGENTS_SOURCE, actor=self.name,\n95\t                                  payload={\"agent\": self.name, \"tier\": effective.label(),\n96\t                                           \"decision\": \"denied\", \"governor\": decision.reason,\n97\t                                           \"of_kind\": p.kind, \"subject\": p.payload.get(\"subject\")},\n98\t                                  parent_id=p.parent_id)\n99\t                res.notes.append(f\"DENIED {p.kind} ({effective.label()}): {decision.reason}\")\n100\t        return res\n101\t"}]},"uuid":"a0a902a0-2e92-4a60-a275-d6726f495370","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:33:16.257Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"59bad103-4d8d-4634-8452-ed4cf267f476","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"b32c4390-31aa-442b-9dd5-e34ede77b057","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"ffbb8a8a-4bb8-4c99-a79e-9ed4dd97a041","agentId":"aa30cb33429fa06f7","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016sLeuEJovmAV731jDMXvWn","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Daily signed checkpoint of the spine head (SIGIL §6.3.6, WARDEN anchor).\n2\t\n3\tGenerates + persists a solo-owner Ed25519 keypair once (1-of-1 trust root), then signs\n4\tthe chain head so the whole spine is anchored: rewriting history would require forging\n5\tthe owner signature, and a shrunk/back-dated head is caught by the monotonic last_seq.\n6\t\n7\tNote: for a personal, single-owner, local-first system the owner's signing key lives\n8\tlocally (0600) — a deliberate simplification of the framework's \"keys never on the\n9\truntime host\" rule, appropriate to this threat model (§1.3). A hardware co-signer can be\n10\tadded later by raising the trust-root threshold.\n11\t\"\"\"\n12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n13\t\n14\timport os\n15\t\n16\tfrom ..config import HEAD_PATH, KEYS_DIR, OWNER_KEY_ID, SCOPE\n17\tfrom ..reuse import (\n18\t    AuthorizerKey,\n19\t    SignedChainHead,\n20\t    TrustRoot,\n21\t    generate_keypair,\n22\t    sign_head,\n23\t    verify_head,\n24\t)\n25\tfrom .store import SpineStore\n26\t\n27\t_PRIV = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.priv\"\n28\t_PUB = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.pub\"\n29\t\n30\t\n31\tdef _owner_keys() -> tuple[str, str]:\n32\t    if not _PRIV.exists():\n33\t        KEYS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n34\t        kp = generate_keypair()\n35\t        _PRIV.write_text(kp.private_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n36\t        os.chmod(_PRIV, 0o600)\n37\t        _PUB.write_text(kp.public_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n38\t    return _PRIV.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip(), _PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n39\t\n40\t\n41\tdef trust_root() -> TrustRoot:\n42\t    _, pub = _owner_keys()\n43\t    return TrustRoot(threshold=1, authorizers=[\n44\t        AuthorizerKey(key_id=OWNER_KEY_ID, name=\"owner\", public_key_b64=pub)])\n45\t\n46\t\n47\tdef checkpoint(store: SpineStore | None = None) -> SignedChainHead:\n48\t    store = store or SpineStore()\n49\t    priv, _ = _owner_keys()\n50\t    head = sign_head(store.entries(), engagement_slug=SCOPE, signers=[(OWNER_KEY_ID, priv)])\n51\t    HEAD_PATH.write_text(head.model_dump_json(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n52\t    return head\n53\t\n54\t\n55\tdef classify_head(head: SignedChainHead, entries: list, tr: TrustRoot) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n56\t    \"\"\"Pure head/chain classification (no globals — testable in isolation). Distinguishes\n57\t    three cases honestly: a shrunk chain (truncation) or a mismatching prefix (history\n58\t    rewrite) are TAMPERING; a chain that merely grew past the anchor is benign — stale.\n59\t    \"\"\"\n60\t    n, signed_n = len(entries), head.entry_count\n61\t    if n < signed_n:\n62\t        return False, f\"TAMPERING: chain has {n} records but the signed head anchors {signed_n} (truncated/rolled back)\"\n63\t    # verify the head against exactly the prefix it signed; append-only ⇒ the prefix is byte-identical.\n64\t    ok, msg = verify_head(head, entries[:signed_n], tr)\n65\t    if not ok:\n66\t        return False, f\"TAMPERING: history rewritten at or below the signed head — {msg}\"\n67\t    if n > signed_n:\n68\t        return True, f\"anchors {signed_n} records; {n - signed_n} appended since — run `sigil sign` to re-anchor\"\n69\t    return True, f\"anchors all {signed_n} records (current)\"\n70\t\n71\t\n72\tdef verify_checkpoint(store: SpineStore | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n73\t    store = store or SpineStore()\n74\t    if not HEAD_PATH.exists():\n75\t        return False, \"no signed head — run `sigil sign` to anchor the spine\"\n76\t    head = SignedChainHead.model_validate_json(HEAD_PATH.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n77\t    return classify_head(head, store.entries(), trust_root())\n78\t"}]},"uuid":"0395a778-065c-4bf0-9484-be088843dc23","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:35:01.294Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b32c4390-31aa-442b-9dd5-e34ede77b057","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}
